To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
elevated levels of Trx in circulation block chemotaxis by interfering directly with neutrophil migration and adhesion.
circulating thioredoxin blocks lipopolysacharide-induced neutrophils chemotaxis by interfering directly with neutrophil activation.

circulating thioredoxin (1) suppresses neutrophil chemokinesis, (2) blocks the in vivo activation of neutrophils, (3) interferes with neutrophil adhesion, and (4) does not alter the in vivo expression of endothelial adhesion molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that regulate Trx levels in the circulation and how these levels influence the outcome of inflammation.
the role of circulating Trx in regulating neutrophil migration and the possible therapeutic implications of this regulation.
the identification and characterization of a novel function of Trx as a circulating chemotaxis suppressor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Trx is a negative modulator of inflammation and that the effects of Trx are dependent on its concentration and time of exposure.
elevated Trx in circulation can suppress neutrophil chemokinesis in response to chemokines and chemotaxis in response to chemotactic agents.
Trx has both positive and negative effects in inflammation, and these effects depend on the timing of Trx elevation and the duration of Trx elevation in circulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Trx is a novel regulator of neutrophil chemokinesis, and that this activity of Trx may have important implications for the pathophysiology of inflammation.
acute elevation of circulating Trx has beneficial effects on inflammation by blocking the recruitment of neutrophils into inflamed tissues.
the beneficial effects of Trx in acute inflammation are likely to be due to its ability to suppress the migration of neutrophils to sites of inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biological effects of Trx depend critically on the duration and level of Trx elevation.
the biological effects of Trx are context dependent and can be either beneficial or deleterious, depending on the duration of the Trx elevation and the disease state.
the effects of Trx in vivo are dependent on both the dose and the duration of Trx exposure.
